nodes.name: Webhook
nodes.notes: Called by IntakeForm.tsx's location autocomplete as the agency types. Payload: { query }. Uses the default response mode (waits for the workflow to finish and responds with the last node's items as a JSON array) since the frontend needs the actual suggestion list back, unlike the fire-and-forget webhooks elsewhere in this project. Confirmed live: omitting responseMode does NOT default to waiting for the last node -- it defaults to an immediate {"message":"Workflow was started"} acknowledgment, so the frontend never got the real data. responseMode is now explicitly set to lastNode so the webhook actually waits and returns what the workflow produces.

nodes.name: Suggest geo targets
nodes.notes: geoTargetConstants:suggest is a global service with no customer-scoped URL path (unlike most Google Ads REST endpoints) and no login-customer-id needed -- same convention build-campaign.json's 'Suggest geo targets' node already relies on.

nodes.name: Format suggestions
nodes.notes: One output item per suggestion (not one item holding an array) so the webhook's default response mode returns a flat JSON array the frontend can use directly. canonicalName (e.g. 'Cambridge,Ontario,Canada') is what gets stored in campaigns.targeted_locations -- fully disambiguated, so build-campaign.json's own later geoTargetConstants:suggest re-lookup at build time resolves it unambiguously instead of a bare city name that could match multiple places. Confirmed live: when this produces exactly one output item, n8n's default webhook response returns it as a bare JSON object rather than a 1-element array -- LocationAutocomplete.tsx normalizes both shapes on its end.
